sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Goewin is a Welsh heroine or goddess. King Math of Wales chose her as his ceremonial footholder. His feet never touched the ground, a mark of a sacred king. The king's nephew Gilfaethwy desired her. His brother Gwydion, a trickster poet, aided the crime. Gilfaethwy raped Goewin. He faced severe punishment. Goewin lost both her virginity and her position. Only an untouched girl could hold the king's feet. In partial amends Math took her as his wife and made her queen.

okr.objective: Record Goewin as the sacred footholder of King Math whose rape cost her the office.
